title: Natural relative Picard presentations and geometric theta characterization
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $B\to S$ an $S$-scheme, $f:C\to B$ a scheme morphism and $g\in\mathbf N$, using truncated natural subtraction $g-1$. For $T\to B$, write $h_T$ for its represented algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A degree-zero Picard presentation of $A\to h_B$ is a family of equivalences, natural in every $B$-scheme $T$, between maps $h_T\to A$ over $h_B$ and sections $x\in\operatorname{Pic}_{C/B}(T)$ whose degree function is identically zero [sk-def-picard-pic], [def-pd-degree-morphism]. When $B=S$, compatibility with a commutative group structure [def-sfb-smooth-integral-group-space] means that multiplication of points represented locally by line modules $L,M$ represents $L\otimes M$.

For pointed spaces $A,D$ over $h_B$, a normalized universal line $P$ on $A\times_{h_B}D$ and a map $\lambda:A\to D$, use the products, axes, small-model module pullbacks and normalized differences of [def-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-data]. A geometric theta characterization of $\lambda$ consists, for every algebraically closed field $K$ and $t:\operatorname{Spec}K\to B$, of an abelian variety $Z/K$ [def-sc-abelian-variety] representing the degree-zero Picard functor of $C_t$ [def-sc-picard-functor], with its tensor group law and its map $Z\to A$ agreeing with the presentation on all scheme tests. For every $p\in C_t(K)$ choose the Picard class $N$ of the ideal of $p$. The degree-$(g-1)$ Hilbert functor [def-pc-hilb-functor] of $C_t$ (its points are the relative effective divisors of degree $g-1$) has a representative $H$ and an Abel map $a:H\to Z$ whose value on every family of effective divisors $E$ is $[\mathcal O(E)\otimes N^{g-1}]$. Its scheme-theoretic image has invertible ideal [def-nagata-invertible-ideal], and its dual ideal [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] is an ample invertible module $L_\Theta$ [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Restricting $P$ along $(j,j\lambda):Z\times_KZ\to A\times_{h_B}D$ gives the normalized difference [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum] of $L_\Theta$, and also that of every translated $L_\Theta$.

The base-change condition means that for each locally Noetherian $T\to S$ [pqf-def-locnoeth], the pulled-back pointed spaces have a Picard presentation identified with that of $C_T$ by the canonical Picard pullback on every test, the pulled-back line has the pulled-back axes and represents the dual, and the unique map between the two pullbacks specified by both projection equations is an isomorphism with the geometric theta characterization. These equations specify identity and iterated-pullback comparisons. For an isomorphism $u:C\simeq C'$ over $S$, Picard transport is the map characterized on all tests by inverse pullback $(u^{-1})^*$. Curve-isomorphism naturality means $a^\vee\lambda_{C'}a=\lambda_C$ for this transport $a$ and the normalized universal-line pullback dual $a^\vee$, for all such isomorphisms, including identities and composites. These are definitions of presentations and compatibility conditions, with no existence asserted.
